title: Band-Resolved Superconducting Gaps via the Thermal Hall Effect in CeRu2
authors: Darian Hall, Luke Pritchard Cairns, Nico Rowland, Yuanqi Lyu, Kohtaro Yamakawa, Josue Rodriguez, Kirin Chanteloup, Didier Perrodin, Joel E. Moore, James G. Analytis
abstract: Standard bulk probes of multiband superconductors cannot assign pairing gaps to specific electron or hole Fermi surfaces. Here we show that thermal Hall transport ($κ_{xy}$), constrained by specific heat and normal-state magnetotransport, resolves this ambiguity in the compensated heavy-fermion superconductor CeRu$_2$. Fixing the gap magnitudes ($Δ_e/k_B\approx 13$K, $Δ_h/k_B\approx 8$K) and band mobilities completely determines the electronic degrees of freedom in $κ_{xx}$ and $κ_{xy}$. A low-field sign reversal in $κ_{xy}$ places the larger gap on the heavy Ce $4f$ electron sheets and the smaller on the hole sheets.
summary: This work uses the thermal Hall effect ($\kappa_{xy}$) in the heavy-fermion superconductor CeRu2 to overcome limitations of standard superconducting probes. By analyzing how $\kappa_{xy}$ changes with magnetic field, the authors definitively assign the larger superconducting gap to the electron-like Ce 4f bands and the smaller gap to the hole bands. This demonstrates a powerful, multi-faceted approach to characterizing multiband superconductivity.
main_problem: Standard bulk probes cannot assign superconducting pairing gaps to specific electron or hole Fermi surfaces in multiband superconductors.
main_result: Thermal Hall transport ($\kappa_{xy}$), combined with specific heat and magnetotransport, uniquely determines the two superconducting gaps, placing the larger gap on the heavy Ce 4f electron sheets.
method: The authors combine multiple transport measurements ($\kappa_{xy}, \kappa_{xx}, C/T$) and theoretical modeling (two-band BCS/BRT theory) to constrain the electronic degrees of freedom.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the compensated heavy-fermion superconductor CeRu2, which exhibits two distinct electronic bands (electron and hole) contributing to superconductivity.
key_observables: Thermal Hall conductivity ($\kappa_{xy}$), specific heat ($C/T$), longitudinal thermal conductivity ($\kappa_{xx}$), and normal-state magnetotransport ($\mu_h/\mu_e$).
important_parameters: Superconducting gaps ($\Delta_e/k_B \approx 13 	ext{ K}$, $\Delta_h/k_B \approx 8 	ext{ K}$), mobility ratio ($\mu_h/\mu_e = 0.68$), and the low-field sign reversal in $\kappa_{xy}$.
main_assumptions: The electronic channel can be modeled as the sum of two independent s-wave BRT contributions, and the analysis relies on the compensation of electron and hole contributions in the normal state.
figures_summary: Figures show specific heat fits to a two-gap model, the dependence of $\kappa_{xy}$ on temperature and field exhibiting a sign reversal, and the decomposition of $\kappa_{xx}$ into electronic and phononic parts.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the ambiguity in gap assignment using bulk probes, then introduces $\kappa_{xy}$ as the diagnostic tool. It uses the combination of $\kappa_{xy}$ with zero-field thermodynamics and magnetotransport to uniquely assign the gaps, concluding with quantitative parameter extraction.
why_interesting: The use of thermal transport ($\kappa_{xy}$) to resolve ambiguities in pairing symmetry and gap structure in strongly correlated materials is a sophisticated diagnostic tool relevant to understanding exotic superconducting states.
